messages.content: Explain self attention.
Self attention lets each token use earlier tokens as context.
What does a tokenizer do.
A tokenizer changes text into token ids for the model.
Explain a context window.
A context window is the earlier token sequence the model can use.
What is a training loss.
Training loss measures how well the model predicts target tokens.
Explain BPE.
BPE merges common token pairs into a larger token vocabulary.
What does an attention head do.
An attention head learns one way to connect earlier tokens.
How does fine tuning work.
Fine tuning makes small changes to a pretrained model for one task.
What is a checkpoint.
A checkpoint saves model weights and tokenizer data for later use.
Explain sampling.
Sampling chooses a next token from model probabilities.
Why use validation data.
This data helps check whether training is generalizing.
Explain embeddings.
Embeddings are learned vectors that represent token ids.
What does a feed forward network do.
A feed forward network transforms each token representation.
What is MPS.
MPS lets PyTorch use Apple GPU hardware on a Mac.
Explain causal masking.
Causal masking stops a token from seeing future tokens.
What does top k sampling do.
Top k sampling limits choices to likely next tokens.
Explain a language model.
A language model predicts the next token in a sequence.
Explain residual connections.
Residual connections add earlier representations to later layers.
What does dropout do.
Dropout hides some values during training to reduce overfitting.
Explain model parameters.
Model parameters are learned values changed during training.
What is an optimizer.
An optimizer changes model parameters using gradients.
Explain self attention.
Self attention uses earlier tokens to build useful context.
Why is that useful.
It helps the model connect words across a sequence.
What is BPE.
BPE builds tokens by merging common pairs.
Why is that useful.
It can make common text use fewer tokens.
